column1: Rooftops covered with grass, vegetable gardens and lush foliage are now a common sight in many cities around the world.
column2: 如今，在世界许多城市，屋顶铺着青草、种着蔬菜或长满繁茂枝叶，已是常见的景象。

column1: More and more private companies and city authorities are investing in green roofs, drawn to their wide-ranging benefits.
column2: 绿色屋顶的种种好处吸引着越来越多的私营企业和城市管理部门为之投资。

column1: Among the benefits are saving on energy costs, mitigating the risk of floods, making habitats for urban wildlife, tackling air pollution and even growing food.
column2: 这些好处包括节省能源开支、降低洪灾风险、为城市野生生物提供栖息地、治理空气污染，甚至还能种出食物。

column1: These increasingly radical urban designs can help cities adapt to the monumental problems they face, such as access to resources and a lack of green space due to development.
column2: 这些日趋大胆的城市设计可以帮助城市适应所面临的巨大难题，例如资源获取问题，以及城市开发导致的绿地不足。

column1: But the involvement of city authorities, businesses and other institutions is crucial to ensuring their success — as is research investigating different options to suit the variety of rooftop spaces found in cities.
column2: 不过，要使这些设计取得成功，市政部门、企业和其他机构的参与至关重要；研究适合城内各种屋顶空间的不同方案也同样重要。

column1: The UK is relatively new to developing green roofs, and local governments and institutions are playing a major role in spreading the practice.
column2: 英国开展屋顶绿化的时间还不算长，地方政府和相关机构在推广这种做法方面发挥着重要作用。
column7: playing a major role in|在……中发挥重要作用

column1: London is home to much of the UK’s green roof market, mainly due to forward-thinking policies such as the London Plan, which has paved the way to more than doubling the area of green roofs in the capital.
column2: 英国绿色屋顶市场的很大一部分集中在伦敦，主要得益于《伦敦规划》等具有前瞻性的政策；这项规划为首都绿色屋顶面积增至原来的两倍多铺平了道路。
column8: more than doubling|增至原来的两倍多

column1: Ongoing research is showcasing how green roofs in cities can integrate with ‘living walls’: environmentally friendly walls which are partially or completely covered with greenery, including a growing medium, such as soil or water.
column2: 正在开展的研究展示了城市绿色屋顶如何与“植物墙”相结合。这种环保墙体部分或全部覆盖着绿色植物，并配有土壤或水等栽培介质。

column1: Research also indicates that green roofs can be integrated with drainage systems on the ground, such as street trees, so that the water is managed better and the built environment is made more sustainable.
column2: 研究还表明，绿色屋顶可以与行道树等地面排水系统结合，从而更好地管理水资源，让建成环境更具可持续性。

column1: There is also evidence to demonstrate the social value of green roofs.
column2: 还有证据可以说明绿色屋顶的社会价值。

column1: Doctors are increasingly prescribing time spent gardening outdoors for patients dealing with anxiety and depression.
column2: 医生越来越常为受焦虑和抑郁困扰的患者开出这样的“处方”：花些时间到户外做园艺。

column1: And research has found that access to even the most basic green spaces can provide a better quality of life for dementia sufferers and help people avoid obesity.
column2: 研究还发现，即使人们能接触到的只是最普通的绿地，也能改善痴呆症患者的生活质量，并帮助人们避免肥胖。

column1: In North America, green roofs have become mainstream, with a wide array of expansive, accessible and food-producing roofs installed in buildings.
column2: 在北美，绿色屋顶已经成为主流。建筑物上建起了各式各样的屋顶，空间宽敞，可供人们进入，还能种出食物。
column4: a wide array of|种类繁多的

column1: Again, city leaders and authorities have helped push the movement forward — only recently, San Francisco, USA, created a policy requiring new buildings to have green roofs.
column2: 同样，城市领导者和主管部门也帮助推动了这一进程。就在不久前，美国旧金山出台了一项政策，规定新建筑必须设有绿色屋顶。
column4: push the movement forward|推动这项行动向前发展

column1: Toronto, Canada, has policies dating from the 1990s, encouraging the development of urban farms on rooftops.
column2: 加拿大多伦多在20世纪90年代就已有相关政策，鼓励在屋顶开发城市农场。

column1: These countries also benefit from having newer buildings than in many parts of the world, which makes it easier to install green roofs.
column2: 这些国家也受益于一个条件：与世界许多地区相比，它们的建筑较新，所以更便于设置绿色屋顶。
column5: parts of the world|世界各地

column1: Being able to keep enough water at roof height and distribute it right across the rooftop is crucial to maintaining the plants on any green roof — especially on ‘edible roofs’ where fruit and vegetables are farmed.
column2: 在屋顶高度储存足够的水，并把水分送到整个屋面，对于养护绿色屋顶上的植物至关重要；种植果蔬的“食用屋顶”尤其如此。
column8: edible roofs|种植食用作物的屋顶

column1: And it’s much easier to do this in newer buildings, which can typically hold greater weight, than to retro-fit old ones.
column2: 在较新的建筑上做到这一点，要比改造老建筑容易得多，因为新建筑通常能承受更大的重量。
column5: hold greater weight|承受更大重量
column6: retro-fit|v. 对既有建筑进行改造

column1: Having a stronger roof also makes it easier to grow a greater variety of plants, since the soil can be deeper.
column2: 承重能力更强的屋顶还可以铺更厚的土层，因此也更容易栽种更多种类的植物。

column1: For green roofs to become the norm for new developments, there needs to be support from public authorities and private investors.
column2: 要让绿色屋顶成为新开发项目的常规做法，公共部门和私人投资者都需要给予支持。

column1: Those responsible for maintaining buildings may have to acquire new skills, such as landscaping, and in some cases, volunteers may be needed to help out.
column2: 负责维护建筑的人可能得掌握景观园艺等新技能，有些情况下还需要志愿者帮忙。
column7: in some cases|在某些情况下

column1: Other considerations include installing drainage paths, meeting health and safety requirements and perhaps allowing access for the public, as well as planning restrictions and disruption from regular activities in and around the buildings during installation.
column2: 其他需考虑的事项包括设置排水通道、达到健康与安全要求，以及是否允许公众进入。还要考虑规划方面的限制，以及施工期间建筑物内外的日常活动可能带来的干扰。

column1: To convince investors and developers that installing green roofs is worthwhile, economic arguments are still the most important.
column2: 要让投资者和开发商相信设置绿色屋顶值得，经济上的理由依然最有说服力。

column1: The term ‘natural capital’ has been developed to explain the economic value of nature; for example, measuring the money saved by installing natural solutions to protect against flood damage, adapt to climate change or help people lead healthier and happier lives.
column2: “自然资本”这个词用来解释大自然的经济价值。例如，可以估算采用自然办法来防范洪灾损失、适应气候变化，或帮助人们过上更健康、更快乐的生活，究竟能省下多少钱。
column6: natural solutions|利用自然的解决办法
column10: lead healthier and happier lives|过上更健康快乐的生活

column1: As the expertise about green roofs grows, official standards have been developed to ensure that they are designed, constructed and maintained properly, and function well.
column2: 随着人们对绿色屋顶的专业知识日益丰富，官方也制定了标准，确保绿色屋顶得到恰当的设计、施工和养护，并能良好运作。

column1: Improvements in the science and technology underpinning green roof development have also led to new variations in the concept.
column2: 支撑绿色屋顶发展的科学与技术取得了进步，也促成了这一概念的多种新形式。

column1: For example, ‘blue roofs’ enable buildings to hold water over longer periods of time, rather than draining it away quickly — crucial in times of heavier rainfall.
column2: 例如，“蓝色屋顶”使建筑物能更长时间地蓄水，而不是把水迅速排走；这一点在雨势较大时尤为关键。
column3: blue roofs|可较长时间蓄水的屋顶

column1: There are also combinations of green roofs with solar panels, and ‘brown roofs’ which are wilder in nature and maximise biodiversity.
column2: 还有些设计把绿色屋顶和太阳能板结合起来，而“棕色屋顶”则更接近自然野生状态，力求最大限度地提高生物多样性。
column5: brown roofs|更接近野生状态的屋顶
column6: wilder|adj. 更接近野生状态的

column1: If the trend continues, it could create new jobs and a more vibrant and sustainable local food economy — alongside many other benefits.
column2: 如果这一趋势延续下去，除了其他诸多好处，还有可能创造新的就业机会，让当地食品经济更有活力，也更可持续。
column4: create new jobs|创造新的就业机会
column7: local food economy|当地食品经济

column1: There are still barriers to overcome, but the evidence so far indicates that green roofs have the potential to transform cities and help them function sustainably long into the future.
column2: 虽然仍有障碍需要克服，但迄今的证据表明，绿色屋顶有潜力改变城市，并帮助它们在未来很长时间里以可持续的方式运转。
column9: function sustainably|以可持续方式运转
column10: long into the future|在未来很长时间里

column1: The success stories need to be studied and replicated elsewhere, to make green, blue, brown and food-producing roofs the norm in cities around the world.
column2: 需要研究这些成功案例，并在其他地方复制推广，才能让绿色屋顶、蓝色屋顶、棕色屋顶和种植食物的屋顶成为世界各地城市的常见做法。
